free_tier.stated: as indexed from the account-setup page: a free trial with 60 concurrent vCPUs, 60 GiB concurrent memory, 10,000 compute-hour credits and a 1 year duration, restricted to NGC organization owners, and the page states that a business email address is required and that personal addresses such as gmail.com are not accepted.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a machine, not an object
per_object_cap.notes: The primary constraint is the virtual machine hardware specification.

retention.stated: the trial must be started by an NGC organization owner behind a non-public domain mailbox, and a trial machine sleep date can be pushed at most 72 hours at a time, so 10,000 compute hours are reachable only by an operator who re-arms a calendar every three days.
retention.notes: a machine record: what is lost is the running process, not a stored object

identity_cost.detail: institution, in the form of a business mailbox: the account-setup page states a business email address is required and that personal addresses such as gmail.com are not accepted, and the trial must be started by an NGC organization owner. A forum report adds that public-suffix addresses such as QQ, Gmail and Outlook are rejected and that a domain mailbox was accepted at signup. No card, hold, phone number or ID document is stated in any evidence row: unknown. The page was read through the search index, not first-party.

evidence.proved: the search index of this page carries the trial table of 60 vCPU, 60 GiB, 10,000 compute hours, 1 year, and the sentence that personal email addresses such as gmail.com are not accepted; a direct broker read of the URL returned the Air user-guide shell instead of the account page, so the table itself was not read first-party in this session

reported, translated: a domain mailbox is required and public-suffix addresses such as QQ, Gmail and Outlook are rejected; the machine needs re-arming every 3 days; 10,000 hours is about 416 days of one vCPU
forum thread titled around using Nvidia's 60c60g machine for free for a year confirms the shape and that a domain mailbox was accepted at signup

counter-report, translated: no stock was available; the token expires immediately; login and machines must be raced for; and a later reply says the machine now sleeps automatically every 24 hours, which contradicts the 72 hour figure

notes: Two independent forum reports disagree on whether the sleep window is 72 hours or 24. DSX Air is a data-centre simulation product, so the machines are network simulators and not a general build host; that is a tooling note and not a rejection. The business-email gate is the finding: this is another institution-shaped free allowance with a five-figure compute-hour number beside it.
